packages.label: דִּבּוּר הַקָּדוֹשׁ וְהַצַּדִּיק הַגָּדוֹל
packages.label_en: Holy Speech and the Great Tzaddik
packages.reason: All five nodes are aspects of the same positive domain: the great tzaddik whose holy mouth utters greatness with dual meaning. The rose (שושנה) and the lips (שפתותיו) are the same as holy speech (דבור הקדוש) — three metaphors for one reality. The ox image (תורי = בכור שורו הדר לו) is the Rebbe's explicit bechina for the great tzaddik (צדיקים הגדולים), and the great tzaddik is the very source of holy speech. Thus all five nodes express the single essential identity: the great tzaddik as the bearer of dual-meaning holy utterance.

merge_notes.reason: Component G (תורי — צדיקים הגדולים) merged into Package 1 because 'תורי' is the Rebbe's image for the great tzaddik ('זֶהוּ בְּחִינַת הַצַּדִּיקִים הַגְּדוֹלִים, בְּחִינַת: בְּכוֹר שׁוֹרוֹ הָדָר לוֹ'). The great tzaddik and his holy speech are two faces of the same reality in this Torah — the great tzaddik IS the one with holy speech of dual meaning. Merging on shared nature (bechina), not cause-effect.

packages.label: צְדָקָה וּמַיִם
packages.reason: All six nodes are different faces of the same essential reality: the flowing, softened, generous heart that gives charity. The Torah explicitly states: צדקה = מים (charity is water), נדיבי לב = בעלי צדקה (generous-hearted = people of charity), and אגם מים = לב רך (pool of water = soft heart ready to give). These are three separate bechina pairs in the dataset but all express the single quality of open-hearted charitable generosity — the softened heart that pours itself out like water.

merge_notes.reason: Component E merged into Package 2 because 'נדיבי לב' and 'בעלי צדקה' are the Torah's explicit bechina: 'שֶׁהַצַּדִּיק מְקַבֵּל דִּבּוּר פִּיו מִנְּדִיבֵי לֵב, דְּהַיְנוּ בַּעֲלֵי צְדָקָה'. These generous-hearted donors share the essential nature of צדקה/מים — they are the human embodiment of the charity-water quality.

Component C merged into Package 2 because 'אגם מים' (pool of water, from 'הַהֹפְכִי הַצּוּר אֲגַם מָיִם') is explicitly equated with 'לב רך' — the soft heart that volunteers for charity ('הַיְנוּ לֵב רַךְ לְהִתְנַדֵּב לִצְדָקָה'). Both are the same quality as מים and צדקה: the flowing, open, giving heart.

packages.label: לֵב אֶבֶן
packages.reason: All four nodes are aspects of the same evil domain: the hardened heart that is closed to charity. 'לב אבן' (stone heart) = 'צור לבבי' (rock of my heart) = 'הצור' (the rock in the verse) = 'אבירי לב הרחוקים מצדקה' (the strong-hearted who are far from charity). These are all the same condition of spiritual hardness, the opposite of the soft, water-flowing heart of Package 2. The Rebbe identifies them explicitly through the verse 'הַהֹפְכִי הַצּוּר אֲגַם מָיִם' — the rock (evil Package 3) needs to be transformed into a pool of water (good Package 2).

packages.label: הַצַּדִּיק הַפָּשׁוּט
packages.reason: גמלא and צדיק הפשוט are two names for the same positive figure: the humble tzaddik who walks in simplicity, does not speak of greatness, and whose entire service is in the domain of silence. The Rebbe derives this from the camel (גמל) metaphor: 'וְלֹא הִלַּכְתִּי בִּגְדֹלוֹת וְנִפְלָאוֹת כְּגָמֻל עֲלֵי אִמּוֹ'. This is a distinct positive figure from the great tzaddik (Package 1): the simple tzaddik is the one who has no parasitic false prophets clinging to him.

packages.label: נָבִיא וּמוֹרֶה שֶׁקֶר
packages.reason: נביא ומורה שקר and זנב are two expressions of the same evil domain: the hypocritical deceiver who mimics the true tzaddik. The Rebbe uses the tail (זנב) as the metaphor for the false prophet — the tail is attached to the ox but is not the ox; it is the parasite that imitates. This is the evil mirror of the great tzaddik (Package 1): Package 1 is the true bearer of holy speech; Package 5 is the one who steals and corrupts that speech.

packages.label: יַבֹּ"ק וְזִוּוּג
packages.reason: All four nodes are aspects of the same spiritual reality: יב"ק (the acronym for יחוד ברכה קדושה — unity, blessing, holiness). 'בקי' is the Aramaic word in the Talmudic dialogue that the Rebbe decodes as יב"ק; 'יבק בקדשה' is the holy dimension of this concept; and 'זווג' (holy union/coupling) is what יבק in holiness actually means — 'בְּחִינַת הַיַּבֹּק בִּקְדֻשָּׁה הוּא בְּחִינַת זִוּוּגִין דִּקְדֻשָּׁה'. All four are the same essential quality of holy union and blessing that flows from proper charity.

merge_notes.reason: Component F (בקי — יב"ק) merged with Component J (יבק בקדשה — זווג) because both pairs refer to the same underlying concept: יב"ק. 'בקי' is the Talmudic word that the Rebbe decodes as an acronym for יב"ק (יחוד ברכה קדושה). 'יבק בקדשה = זווג' is the holy meaning of that same יב"ק. Two components, one reality.
